title: crosslang sdks: surface credential hints and stream helper ergonomics
author: Ethan Morris
description: Summary: Introduce a small, ergonomic surface across the Python/TypeScript/Go SDK packages that makes credential hints and stream consumer wiring simpler for application code. Motivation: customers repeatedly ask for clearer token lifecycle guidance and helper hooks that let applications opt-in to lightweight session leases and prefetch heartbeat semantics without embedding runtime-specific logic. This PR implements: 1) A CredentialHints struct/option (Python: CredentialHints, TS: CredentialHintsOptions, Go: CredentialHints) that allows callers to provide non-sensitive metadata (e.g., 'product', 'purpose', 'session_ttl_hint') that the connector and orchestrator can use to improve warmup/route decisions. 2) A StreamHelpers module with a small set of helpers: auto_retry_iterable (py), streamReconnectHelper (ts), and StreamGuard (go) to centralize backoff/coalesce behavior, expose a typed on_reconnect callback, and standardize graceful shutdown semantics across SDKs. 3) A session lease helper (opt-in) that surfaces lease_acquired/lease_revoked callbacks and a light-weight heartbeat utility used by Redwood Private deployments; it's documented as opt-in and off by default. 4) Version bumps for the SDK package artifacts in the monorepo: python 0.9.3 -> 0.9.4, typescript 1.6.1 -> 1.6.2, go 1.5.2 -> 1.5.3. Backwards compatibility: All public constructors keep existing signatures; new helpers are additive and guarded behind new exports (no breaking change). See Linear ENG-2042/ENG-2077 for product acceptance criteria. Checklist: - [x] API surface reviewed for backwards compatibility - [x] Unit tests for helpers (all three SDKs) - [x] Integration smoke test exercising session lease flow against local emulator - [x] Docs updates and quickstart snippet - [x] Version bumps and changelogs updated High level commit list: - feat: add CredentialHints option and wire into connector payloads - feat: introduce StreamHelpers + common backoff profiles - feat: session lease callbacks and heartbeat util - test: add unit/integration tests across python/ts/go - docs: add credential hints guide + sample code - chore: bump package versions and changelogs Commits (summary): - a1b9f2e feat(sdk): add CredentialHints option and serialization hooks - 3c4d1ef feat(stream): introduce reconnect helper and backoff presets - 7d2be44 feat(session): session lease callbacks + heartbeat util - 9f8aa21 test: add coverage for retry windows and reconnect logic - e2c7d55 docs: add credential hints guide and quickstart snippet - f6b9f00 chore: bump sdk package versions and changelogs Changed areas (high-level): - packages/sdk-python/redwood_sdk/credentials.py (CredentialHints, docs) - packages/sdk-python/tests/test_stream_helpers.py - packages/sdk-typescript/src/stream/helpers.ts - packages/sdk-typescript/src/auth/credentialHints.ts - packages/sdk-go/cred/credential_hints.go - packages/sdk-go/stream/stream_guard.go - packages/sdk-go/stream/stream_guard_test.go - docs/sdk/credential-hints.md - docs/sdk/streaming-helpers.md - examples/session-lease-quickstart (python + ts) Testing/CI notes: - CI matrix covers python, node, go lint/tests. - One flaky integration test (python::test_stream_retry_backoff) failed on first run due to a race in the local emulator; rerun passed. - All linters and type checks pass. - Coverage diff: +0.6% across SDK packages. Deployment/rollout notes: - This is a purely additive change. No server changes required. Server may consume CredentialHints metadata immediately but will ignore missing hints. Docs + changelogs included. Links: Linear ENG-2042 (credential hints), ENG-2077 (stream ergonomics). Related PRs: none (introduces new helpers). Reviewers, please see the "examples/session-lease-quickstart" folder for minimal consumption samples for each language. Merge plan: squash merge after approvals, small follow-up hotfix expected for edge-case around reconnect cancellation (tracked ENG-2099).

review_comments: Priya Nair: Overall this looks great — small ask: can we make the credential hints validation logic explicit (e.g., enforce max length) so we don't rely on downstream enforcement?
